# Tokyo Family Trip Plan: 5 Days, 2 Adults + 1 Child

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg

A relaxed Tokyo plan focused on easy transit, one museum day, one park day, and a kid-friendly sushi experience. I’ve kept the pacing family-friendly and budgeted for a total trip spend of about **USD 3,200 excluding international flights**.

## Best Family-Friendly Base Areas

| Area | Why it works | Transit fit | Typical 3-star+ family hotel range/night |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ueno | Easy airport access, parks, museums, calmer pace | JR + subway access | USD 140–240 |
| Asakusa | Classic sights, simple navigation, family atmosphere | Subway + sightseeing lines | USD 130–230 |
| Shinjuku (west side) | Many hotel choices, strong rail network | Major subway/JR hub | USD 160–280 |
| Tokyo Station / Marunouchi | Very convenient for day trips and transfers | Best rail connectivity | USD 180–320 |

Recommended base: **Ueno or Asakusa** for the best balance of cost, family comfort, and easy sightseeing.

## 5-Day Tokyo Itinerary and Cost Plan

| Day | Plan | Estimated Cost for 3 | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Apr 10 | Arrival, check-in, Asakusa stroll, early dinner | USD 220–320 | Light first day; keep it close to hotel |
| Apr 11 | Easy city sightseeing: Senso-ji, Ueno area, Ameyoko | USD 180–280 | Mostly walking and short train rides |
| Apr 12 | Museum day: Tokyo National Museum + Ueno Park | USD 160–260 | Best low-stress indoor day |
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/31/2014_02_08_ueno.jpg Alt=| Apr 12 | Museum day: Tokyo National Museum + Ueno Park | USD 160–260 | Best low-stress indoor day |, Tokyo, Japan
| Apr 13 | Park day: Shinjuku Gyoen or Ueno Park + playground time | USD 150–240 | Good downtime day for child |
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f8/Footbridge_over_a_pond_in_Shinjuku_Gyoen_National_Garden_and_NTT_DoCoMo_Yoyogi_Building%2C_Tokyo%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=| Apr 13 | Park day: Shinjuku Gyoen or Ueno Park + playground time | USD 150–240 | Good downtime day for child |, Tokyo, Japan
| Apr 14 | Kid-friendly sushi meal + Odaiba or Tokyo Bay area | USD 240–380 | Sushi lunch/dinner plus simple waterfront time |
| Departure Apr 15 | Check-out, airport transfer | USD 70–150 | Depends on airport and train/taxi choice |

## Day-by-Day Family Itinerary

### Day 1: Arrival and Easy Asakusa Evening
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Afternoon: Arrive, take airport transfer, check in, rest.
- Evening: Short walk around **Asakusa** and **Senso-ji** area for a gentle first taste of Tokyo.
- Food: Casual ramen, curry rice, or a family set meal near the hotel.

### Day 2: Classic Tokyo Sights
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/signpost-split.svg
- Morning: Visit **Senso-ji**, Nakamise shopping street, and nearby photo stops.
- Afternoon: Head to **Ueno** for Ameyoko market streets and a relaxed city walk.
- Food: Try a simple tempura, udon, or teishoku lunch with child-friendly options.

### Day 3: Museum Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/book.svg
- Morning: **Tokyo National Museum** in Ueno; choose the main galleries and keep it short.
- Afternoon: Break in **Ueno Park** or nearby cafes; optional small zoo stop if energy is good.
- Food: Museum-area lunch with rice bowls, noodles, or curry; easy for kids.

### Day 4: Park Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Spend time in **Shinjuku Gyoen** or return to **Ueno Park** for open space and walking.
- Afternoon: Add a playground, snack break, and a low-key shopping stop if desired.
- Food: Bakery lunch, sandwich cafe, or family restaurant with high chairs and kids’ menus.

### Day 5: Kid-Friendly Sushi and Waterfront Time
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
- Morning: Easy start with a slow breakfast and one last neighborhood walk.
- Afternoon: Visit **Odaiba** or Tokyo Bay for simple indoor-outdoor sightseeing.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/34/Chiba_prefecture%2C_Tokyo_Bay%2C_Kawasaki%2C_seen_from_Shibuya_Stream.jpg Alt=Afternoon: Visit **Odaiba** or Tokyo Bay for simple indoor-outdoor sightseeing, Tokyo, Japan
- Food: Book a **kid-friendly sushi meal** at a conveyor-belt or casual sushi chain with cooked items, tamago, udon, and small plates.

## Budget Breakdown for USD 3,200 Total

| Category | Estimated Total | Target Range |
|---|---:|---:|
| Hotel, 5 nights | USD 900–1,300 | 3-star family room or two-room setup |
| Local transport | USD 120–220 | Subway, airport transfer, occasional taxi |
| Food and drinks | USD 650–900 | Mix of casual meals and one nicer sushi meal |
| Attractions and museum entries | USD 80–180 | Mostly low-cost sightseeing |
| Snacks, convenience items, extras | USD 120–220 | Child snacks, drinks, small purchases |
| Buffer | USD 300–500 | For price swings and flexibility |

Target total: **USD 2,170–3,320**
Best-fit plan: aim for **USD 2,700–3,000** so you stay comfortably under budget.

## Hotel Shortlist Criteria

Choose a hotel that matches most of these:
- 3-star or better
- Family room or twin + extra bed
- Within 5–10 minutes of a subway or JR station
- Elevator, laundry access, and breakfast available
- Quiet neighborhood or upper-floor room request
- Walking distance to convenience stores and family restaurants

Good search focus:
- **Ueno/Asakusa** for value
- **Tokyo Station/Marunouchi** for maximum convenience
- **Shinjuku** if you want more hotel inventory and dining variety

## Booking Checklist for Tokyo

- Confirm hotel room type for **2 adults + 1 child**
- Check whether the child sleeps free, needs a bed, or shares bedding
- Verify station distance and whether the route has an elevator
- Reserve airport transfer or plan train route from arrival airport
- Book museum tickets only if timed entry is needed
- Add one sushi reservation for a family-friendly spot
- Check hotel breakfast hours and child pricing
- Save offline maps for the hotel, station, and key attractions
- Pack a light stroller or carrier if your child may get tired
- Keep one flexible afternoon in case of weather or jet lag
